title: Strengths and limitations of forms of government in Ethiopia
competency: Identify the strengths and limitations of each form of government in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: A form of government where the state is ruled by citizens' representatives chosen in periodic elections.

en.text: Every form of government has strengths and limitations. The monarchy built the state, modernized, defended sovereignty at Adwa and gave the 1931 Constitution, but ignored diversity and kept power by descent. The Derg united the country, gave land to the tiller and ran literacy campaigns, but committed gross rights violations like the Red Terror. The post-1991 government brought self-determination and infrastructure, but with implementation problems and conflicts.

screens.title: A perfect government?
screens.ask: Can any form of government be completely free of limitations?
opts: No: every government has strengths and limitations
screens.after: The book says governments in Ethiopia, like any others, have strengths and limitations.

paras: Strengths and limitations as the book gives them:
table: State formation; modernization; Adwa victory; diplomacy (AU in Addis Ababa); 1931 Constitution
Ignored diversity; power by descent; state religion; no party system
National unity ("Ethiopia First"); land to the tiller; literacy campaigns; equality of cultures; secularism
Red Terror and gross rights violations; wars; one-party system
Self-determination; language and cultural rights; representation; infrastructure; secularism
Not genuine in implementation; extremism, conflicts and displacement
